name: The Brimstone Seep

detectability.signature: A sulfurous yellow-white radiance leaking along a straight corridor, paired with impossible subspace harmonics that no natural source produces.

proximity: Subspace radios pick up fragmentary transmissions from ships that never existed
Hull plating develops a faint warm glow as higher-dimensional radiation bleeds through
contact: Entering the corridor displaces vessels partially out of normal space; hulls flicker and phase
Crew experience severe vertigo as local geometry refuses to stay consistent
prolonged_exposure: Matter held in the seep dissolves back into hyperspace, crew and vessel together
Survivors of brief exposure report lasting sensory anomalies and dreams of elsewhere

phenomena: Visible discharge of yellow-white energy along the corridor axis
Subspace interference patterns resembling structured signal traffic
Objects exiting at different locations than entered when skirting the boundary
hazards: Dimensional displacement of crew and vessel into hyperspace
Reality breakdown: localized physics becomes unreliable within the corridor
Complete ship destruction during bleed surges
opportunities: Communication with other dimensions/times via structured subspace leakage
Shortcut through normal space for shielded drones riding the corridor's calm edge
Recovery of lost ships/personnel: objects swallowed by the seep occasionally surface intact
known_incidents: The Ketchuan Institute's experimental jump array failed catastrophically in 2214, birthing the Seep and erasing the station with all hands
Freighter Marrowlight was swallowed whole in 2396 and reappeared nine light-years away four years later, crew missing, cargo untouched
description: The Brimstone Seep is a wound in the fabric of normal space: a straight, corridor-shaped fissure four thousand kilometers long that glows a sulfurous yellow-white, like light forced through molten glass. It has no source and casts no shadows, simply leaking radiance from somewhere adjacent to reality. Sensors hear it long before eyes find it, as layered subspace harmonics that repeat like something practicing speech.

The seep is widening, millimeter by measured kilometer, its boundaries flexing in violent surges that follow no schedule. Ships that graze the corridor phase partway out of normal space, their hulls flickering between two states while instruments report contradictory positions. The freighter Marrowlight entered one end of the seep in 2396 and exited nowhere near it, four years and nine light-years later.

The wound is not natural. Archival records identify it as the death of the Ketchuan Institute's deep-range jump array, whose test firing in 2214 tore a permanent channel into hyperspace and took the station's hundred researchers with it. Two centuries of study have established only what the seep does, never how to close it, and every containment proposal has failed at the simulation stage.

Today the corridor is ringed by automated warning buoys and a permanent research hulk parked at maximum safe distance, listening to the structured signals that leak through. Some of those signals match voices from ships lost elsewhere, decades after their disappearances. The seep grows a little each year, and the standing fleet directive remains simple: observe, record, and keep everything else away.
